noise_why: canary-pwr's registered band, 10: docs/roadmap/prereg/K09.json `noise.canary-pwr` = 10 (its source: 'N02: canary-pwr variants' +-10', docs/roadmap/tasks/archive/N02-keep-rule-for-defaults.md), carried unchanged into docs/roadmap/prereg/K09.9-rerun.json (the plugin's headless path on canary-pwr with the K09 fix-ups) and every N05 and N06 canary-pwr row; routing-quality.md's totals rule: 'until it is measured, max(2, 5 % of the board's connections), and 10 for canary-pwr'. Why a band and not K13's 0: the two arms give the router different input bytes (KiCad's export against the reader, K13.2's rounding, fixed wires made from pcbnew's fill polygons against the snapshot's filled_polygon), and routing-quality.md says that on canary-pwr 'a small input change moves completion by about +-10 unrouted connections'. With one board the set noise is sqrt(10^2) = 10, so the gate's no-regress total clause is keep_rule's clause (2) exactly: kicad_pcb - dsn <= 10; its per-board clause (worse than 2 x 10) is looser and decides nothing here. min_boards stays 3 because the parser refuses less (gate_totals.rs: 'not below 3'); the three-board minimum is for keep decisions, this registration decides no default (decides_no_default), so the gate's 'REFUSED ... N=1' line is expected and is not a failure of the rule (keep_rule_by_hand)

metric_definitions.via_in_pad: summary via_in_pad: tools/kicad-oracle/via_in_pad.py's vias_in_pads on the routed board minus the input board's, floored at 0 (the demos' own vias in pads are not routing's); a hard metric because the gate requires it (D8: a via in a pad is a failure)
metric_definitions.below_minimum: summary below_minimum: routed tracks and vias (those whose nanometre copper key, oracle_lib.copper_key, the input board does not have) narrower than the Board Setup minimum track width, with a diameter under the minimum via diameter or a drill under the minimum through-hole drill (kicad_steps.py stats' board_minimums_mm), summed
metric_definitions.manufacturing_breaches: summary manufacturing_breaches: the routing-caused KiCad DRC items (oracle_lib.summarize with both boards' copper, Q22.2: an item is routing-caused when it involves a track or via the input board does not have at the same nanometre coordinates, width, layer and net) of the types clearance, hole_clearance, hole_to_hole, copper_edge_clearance, track_width, via_diameter, annular_width, drill_out_of_range, solder_mask_bridge, shorting_items, summed. The other routing-caused types are in routing_caused_by_type
metric_definitions.kicad_unconnected: summary unconnected: kicad-cli's unconnected_items on the routed board
metric_definitions.errors_by_type: summary violations: every DRC item of severity error on the routed board, by type (copper classes forced to error), pre-existing ones included
metric_definitions.prepare_load_seconds: summary prepare_s + load_s: the plugin's export or snapshot (headless pcbnew) plus the router's `-de FILE -drc` (parse, build, check)
metric_definitions.input_unconnected: summary input_unconnected: kicad-cli's unconnected_items on the input board as given
metric_definitions.via_in_pad_raw: summary via_in_pad_raw, the routed board's count with the input's vias in pads

A run that fails (a), (b) or (c) did not measure K14: it is recorded, not judged, and repeats only after the fix, under an amendment
keep_rule: K14.6's Accept clauses for the measurement, all three: (1) guards: in both arms manufacturing_breaches = 0, below_minimum = 0 and via_in_pad = 0, absolutely, not 'no worse than the other arm' (decided 2026-10-20: routing never breaks the board's manufacturing rules; routing-quality.md, order of importance items 1 and 2); (2) unconnected: kicad_pcb's kicad_unconnected is at most dsn's + 10 (noise_why); (3) both arms' session_sha256 (summary.json) are recorded in K14.6's note. An arm that is aborted or not graded fails (1) and (2). K14.6's fourth clause, the owner's Route inside KiCad, is not measured here (decision_table)
keep_rule_by_hand: the gate cannot judge one board (its three-board minimum), so K14.6 applies keep_rule by hand from OUT/dsn/canary-pwr/summary.json and OUT/kicad_pcb/canary-pwr/summary.json. The gate is run for its checks only: `freerouting-dev gate --records records.json --baseline baseline.json --prereg docs/roadmap/prereg/K14.json --write-baseline`, then `freerouting-dev gate --records records.json --baseline baseline.json --prereg docs/roadmap/prereg/K14.json --all-pairs` (K13.json amendment 1: --all-pairs needs --baseline), where records.json carries per arm the metrics above from summary.json and the input sha256. Its HARD lines of both pairs are clause (1); its 'totals verdict' with set noise 10 is clause (2); its 'REFUSED ... N=1' line is the three-board minimum and is expected; anything else it prints is reported, not judged
on_failure: decided 2026-10-20 (routing-quality.md, order of importance item 1, and K14.6's Accept): a routing-caused manufacturing breach, below-minimum copper or a via in a pad in either arm blocks K14.6, which stays [~] naming the items. A kicad_pcb breach that dsn does not have is a defect of K14.1-K14.4 or of the snapshot path; one in both arms, or in dsn only, is a defect of the shared code or of the DSN path, named as such. The fix lands as an item of its own, then this run repeats at the fixed commit under an amendment that names the fix, with nothing else changed. 'Fix gains, don't remove them' (decided 2026-10-20, Q18) applies: a kicad_pcb arm that routes better but breaches gets the breach fixed and is measured again; the K14 settings are not removed, and these boards are not sent back to the DSN to dodge a guard. Clause (2) failing (kicad_pcb more than 10 above dsn) keeps K14.6 [~] with the difference explained, and is handled the same way
decides_no_default: this registration decides no default: K14's four settings stay off by default under both profiles (K14's Design), board_input's default stays kicad_pcb under enhanced (K13.7) whatever this run shows, and no ENHANCED entry changes. It checks that a board's saved DSN fix-ups route on the default input as well as on the DSN

decision_table.met: K14.6's note records the per-arm table, validity (a)-(c) and both session sha256s; K14.6 becomes [x] only once the owner's confirmation from a Route inside KiCad on canary-pwr, with its saved options, on the snapshot, is recorded too
decision_table.not met: K14.6 stays [~] naming the clause that failed and its items (on_failure)

report: per arm: kicad_unconnected (and input_unconnected), errors_by_type, routing_caused_by_type, manufacturing_breaches, below_minimum and below_minimum_by_kind, via_in_pad, prepare_load_seconds (prepare_s + load_s), route_seconds, aborted, session_sha256, design_sha256, args_sha256 and whether the grade is shared; validity (a)-(c) with the fixed-wire and dropped-plane counts each arm's args.json log reports; the routing-caused items of each arm that also appear on the input board at the same place and type (pre-existing violations counted again on copper the round trip re-laid, K13.2), named, not subtracted
known_effects: both arms import the session whole, as the plugin does (fix_existing is off in the saved file): ImportSpecctraSES deletes the board's unlocked tracks and vias and adds the session's, and places the footprints. Existing copper comes back at the router's resolution, and copper that moved by even 1 nm counts as routing-caused on the copper basis. The fixed wires are in neither session (K14.4's route test; the DSN path's property), so the pours they stand for are refilled from the zones after the import in both arms. The two arms' fixed wires come from different fill sources (pcbnew's polygons against the snapshot's filled_polygon) and may differ within the bound K14.4's note gives; that is part of what is measured
stop_rule: one registered run per arm; no reruns with other settings; an aborted arm is recorded and not rerun. A rerun at a fixed commit after a guard or validity failure is an amendment naming the fix (on_failure). Any change after the first number goes in `amendments` with its reason
